market.headline: Tech is flat so far today after two weeks of AI selling. The 10-year yield has climbed to 5.15 and the VIX is at 19.3. Nvidia reports today under an interim CEO, and that report sets the next move for every chip and AI stock on this page.
watch: NVDA results due today (date is an estimate, no time confirmed)
QQQ 660.48 yesterday's low, then 647.05, the 20-day low
SPY 738.07 yesterday's low, then 729.58, the 200-day average
market.if_then: If QQQ trades below 660.48 (yesterday's low), then make no new tech buys today and keep cash for after Nvidia's report.

stocks.headline: Reports today with interim CEO Colette Kress after Jensen Huang's exit. The stock is down 28.1% in 20 sessions to 156.14.
stocks.why: The business is not the problem. Sales are up 106% and speeding up, operating margin is 65%, and forecasts rose 23% in 90 days. The stock trades at 10× next year's profit, its cheapest in 5 years. It fell anyway on Huang's resignation, a spying scandal and tighter export controls. Beats are already expected: it fell after 5 of the last 8, so a beat alone won't lift it. What matters tonight is the outlook, the damage from export controls, data-centre demand, and a clear plan for a permanent CEO. A clean report lifts MU, TSM, AVGO, ARM, SMCI, CRWV, AMD and QQQ. A vague outlook or leadership drama drags all of them to new lows.

long_term.reason: Earnings power is intact and the price is the lowest in years, but the leadership crisis is unresolved. Keep what you own and don't add until the new management proves itself.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A firm outlook plus a named permanent CEO turns this into Add on dips. Lost China or data-centre orders turn it into Trim.
stocks.action: Don't buy ahead of the report. Hold your shares through it and decide tomorrow on the outlook, not the beat.

levels.means: above = sellers are exhausted ahead of the report; below = the slide is still on
above = yesterday's floor holds; below = heading for the low
above = the 52-week low holds; below = new lows, don't catch it

stocks.if_then: If it trades below 148.8 before the report, then don't buy the drop. Wait for the results.

stocks.headline: Down 52.7% from its high, now 119.75, up 0.6% so far today, with a $664.0B order backlog.
stocks.why: This is the cheapest way on this page to own the AI build-out. It trades at 11× next year's profit with sales up 30% and speeding up, and it has beaten forecasts 4 quarters in a row. The sell-off is about fear that AI data-centre spending will slow, not about Oracle's own numbers. The real risk is cost: building data centres for that backlog eats cash, and analysts expect profit per share to fall from a year ago when it reports Dec 14. A weak Nvidia report hits it with the rest of AI infrastructure. A strong one makes it a top rebound candidate.

long_term.reason: A huge backlog, growth that is speeding up, and the lowest valuation in 5 years. This agrees with the house view.

stocks.what_would_change_it: Cancelled or delayed backlog, or Nvidia signalling a data-centre slowdown, would move this to Wait.
stocks.action: Buy a half position now at about 119.75. Add the second half only after Nvidia's report, if it still holds 118.25.

levels.means: above = the buy holds; below = stop adding, the 52-week low is next
above = floor intact; below = the long-term case needs re-checking
above = the rebound is real (20-day average); below = still in the downtrend

stocks.if_then: If it falls below 118.25 today, then stop buying and wait for 109.21 to add.
